newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt feel heat on EMU worries, French vote.
newsitem.headline: German debt feel heat on EMU worries, French vote.

text.p: Increasing worries about the future of European monetary union and Sunday's election victory by the French left-wing weighed on German Bunds and futures in early trading on Monday.

The market showed little chance for advancement as traders said the weekend clash between Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer and the Bonn government increased the risk for a delay in currency union, slated for January 1, 1999.
They also said Sunday's stronger-than-expected victory by the French left-wing in the election has also spooked the market and fostered doubts about the strength of the euro.
At 0715 GMT, DTB June Bund futures were down eight basis points at 100.61 points but off the session low at 100.43 points reached at the outset of dealings.
The 10-year 6.00 percent benchmark cash Bund due July 2007 was trading at 100.36 percent with a yield of 5.94 percent compared with the close on Friday at 100.43 percent.

"The market is a bit surprised at the strength of the socialist victory in France," said one trader at broker Trinkaus Capital Markets in Duesseldorf, noting he expected range trade for the session with a downside bias.

Traders noted the market had factored in a left-wing victory that would prompt investors to view the new currency with scepticism since the left-wing will likely favour a flexible, if not lax, interpretation of EMU entry criteria.

But Bunds found support by growing prospects for a delay in currency union after the Bundesbank said on Sunday it stood by the Maastricht Treaty and would fight Bonn's plans to revalue the bank's reserves to untap profits to cut its deficit.
"The general market feeling is that the Bundesbank will win this fight in the end," said one trader. "That will be extremely positive. But dealings right now are very negative."

Traders said the market was starting to price in a delay in currency union, a question Germany's Der Spiegel magazine said Tietmeyer has begun to raise but one the Bundesbank denied the central bank chief has voiced.
MMS International said June Bund futures risked falling to 100.33738 and that the market's refusal to rebreak 101.00 has signaled a head and shoulders formation on daily chart.
"That suggests further downside correction for the coming sessions," MMS said, noting upside risk was confined to 100.86 and that 100.28 would provide support before the 100.00 level.
